CHATBOT.TITLE: Chatbot
CHATBOT.SUBTITLE: The Twitch chat of the channels that picked this server as their home.
CHATBOT.OK_ABGEGLICHEN: The chat connection has been synced.
CHATBOT.OK_PROBE: The test message is on its way. If it does not show up in chat, this card will say so shortly.
CHATBOT.F_KEIN_HEIM: This server is not the home of any channel.
CHATBOT.F_ABGEBROCHEN: Nothing was synced. The reason is in the card below.
CHATBOT.F_KANAL: The ID for this channel was missing. Nothing was changed.
CHATBOT.F_AUS: The live announcement is switched off. Nothing was sent.
CHATBOT.F_ZU_LANG: The text is too long. Twitch accepts 500 characters at most.
CHATBOT.F_PLATZHALTER: It contains a placeholder that does not exist. It would appear literally in chat.
CHATBOT.F_NUR_DISCORD: {rolle} and {dauer} only exist in the Discord announcement. In Twitch chat they would just be plain text.
CHATBOT.F_TECHNISCH: That failed for a technical reason. The log has the details.
CHATBOT.LEER_TITEL: No channel has picked this server as its home
CHATBOT.LEER_TEXT: A channel's chatbot is managed from exactly one Discord server. The channel owner makes that choice in their profile under "Connected accounts".
CHATBOT.WARUM_TEXT: A Twitch channel's chatbot is managed from exactly one Discord server: the one the channel owner picked. Other servers can follow and announce the stream, but not configure its chat. That way nobody can change someone else's chat settings just because they have permissions here.
CHATBOT.MOD_ZUERST: The chat is only subscribed once the bot is a moderator.
CHATBOT.NICHTS_EMPFANGEN: nothing received yet. The channel is probably quiet.
CHATBOT.NAECHSTER_ABGLEICH: The next sync will take care of it.
CHATBOT.SCHREIBT_ALS: The chatbot writes under the name {{name}}, not under a bot name. Anyone reading the announcement sees it as if {{name}} had typed it.
CHATBOT.NOCH_NICHT_ERLAUBT: This is not allowed yet. Switching it on therefore does nothing: only {{name}} can allow it, in their own profile under Connected accounts → Permissions.
CHATBOT.ERLAUBT_UNKLAR: Whether it is allowed cannot be determined right now.
CHATBOT.NICHT_NOCHMAL: {{wann}}. It will not be retried: a chat message cannot be taken back, and five identical ones would be worse than none.
CHATBOT.UNGEWISS_TEXT: Started {{wann}}. Whether it arrived can no longer be determined. Nothing will be resent.
CHATBOT.HOECHSTENS: {{n}} characters at most. Twitch does not accept more.
CHATBOT.ANSAGE_TEXT: When the stream starts, the bot says so in Twitch chat.
CHATBOT.KEIN_ABGLEICH: No sync has run yet. The daily run will catch up, or you can trigger it here.
CHATBOT.ABGEBROCHEN: Aborted: {{grund}}. Nothing was subscribed or unsubscribed.
CHATBOT.SOLL_IST: {{soll}} channel chat(s) should be connected, {{ist}} subscription(s) exist at Twitch.
CHATBOT.OHNE_CONDUIT: Without a conduit no chat can be subscribed.
CHATBOT.ABGLEICH_TEXT: Anyone who just typed /mod does not have to wait for the next daily run.
CHATBOT.FUSSNOTE: What the bot does in chat: It reads along, answers “My commands”, posts “My announcements”, takes raffle entries and song requests under “Join in”, and announces the stream start if that is switched on. Chat protection is still a draft. The bot does not store the text of a message: it reads it, replies and forgets it. Only !los and song requests keep the sender (Twitch name and ID), because they cannot work without it — raffle entries for 30 days, song requests for 7 days, after which the daily run deletes them.

ANSAGEN.F_TEXT: Without text the announcement has nothing to say.
ANSAGEN.F_ZU_LANG: Twitch chat accepts 500 characters at most.
ANSAGEN.F_PLATZHALTER: It contains a placeholder that does not exist. It would appear literally in chat.
ANSAGEN.F_NUR_DISCORD: {rolle} and {dauer} only work in Discord, not in Twitch chat.
ANSAGEN.F_INTERVALL: The interval must be between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes.
ANSAGEN.F_ZEILEN: The number of chat lines must be between 0 and {{max}}.
ANSAGEN.F_KANAL: This guild has no channel whose chat the bot may write in.
ANSAGEN.F_TECHNISCH: That failed for a technical reason. The log has the details.

ANSAGEN.TITLE: My announcements
ANSAGEN.SUBTITLE: What the bot writes in your chat on its own, under your name.
ANSAGEN.WANN_1: Only while you are live: the bot writes nothing into an empty chat. And only when enough time has passed since the last announcement and enough has happened in chat. The second condition is the difference between a bot and a vending machine: set the number to 0 and it talks into the silence too.
ANSAGEN.WANN_2: If more than one announcement is due at the same time, one per round goes out: the one that has waited longest. Otherwise a whole block would arrive at once.
ANSAGEN.LIVE_TEXT: The one-time announcement at stream start already exists. It is set up under "My channel" because it belongs to the channel, not to this list.
ANSAGEN.ANLEGEN_TEXT: Your Discord, your YouTube, your rules: whatever should recur during the stream.
ANSAGEN.EINE_ZEILE: A chat message is one line: line breaks become spaces.
ANSAGEN.BAUSTEINE_VOR: You create your own snippets such as
ANSAGEN.ABSTAND_HILFE: At least {{min}} minutes: the bot writes to all channels with one account, and Twitch adds that up.
ANSAGEN.NUR_WENN: Only when something is going on
ANSAGEN.NUR_WENN_HILFE: This many chat messages must have arrived since the last announcement. 0 means always.
ANSAGEN.LEER_TEXT: Create one, for example a pointer to your Discord every 25 minutes. It only goes out while you are live.

STATISTIK.TITLE: Statistics
STATISTIK.SUBTITLE: How the stream went, from Twitch's own lists.
STATISTIK.SPEICHERT_1: Everything here comes from Twitch at this very moment: the same lists your Twitch dashboard shows. We keep no copy; once you close the page, none of it stays with us.
STATISTIK.SPEICHERT_2: That is why loading takes a moment, and why there is no history here: whatever Twitch does not keep (who came how often, who wrote how much) we would have to record, and that is exactly what we do not do.
STATISTIK.EIGENE_ZEILE: From our own record, not fetched from Twitch.
STATISTIK.EIN_STREAM: This is one stream, not a history: the record is overwritten at the next start. A summary across several streams would need its own table.
STATISTIK.FOLLOWER_LEER_TEXT: As soon as someone follows you, they appear here.
STATISTIK.ABOS_TEXT: Without you: Twitch lists you in your own list.
STATISTIK.ABOS_LEER_TEXT: As soon as someone subscribes to you, they appear here.
STATISTIK.BITS_TEXT: Comes straight from Twitch with rank and score. We calculate nothing.
STATISTIK.BITS_LEER_TEXT: As soon as someone sends Bits, Twitch creates a leaderboard.
STATISTIK.NOCH_NICHT: Not included yet: raids, because those events pass through the inbox and are not kept after processing. And a summary across several streams, which would need its own table. Both are noted in the plan so they do not count as available.

BEFEHLE.TITLE: My commands
BEFEHLE.SUBTITLE: What the bot replies when someone types something in your chat.
BEFEHLE.EIGEN_TEXT: You set the word, for example {{p}}rules, and the text the bot replies with.
BEFEHLE.HAEUFIG: Common: rules, discord, social, donate. {{p}}discord is deliberately not a built-in command: only you know your invite link.
BEFEHLE.LIVE_EINS: stays empty while you are not live. Word the sentence so it still works: Live for {uptime} rather than just {uptime}.
BEFEHLE.LIVE_VIELE: stay empty while you are not live. Word the sentence so it still works: Live for {uptime} rather than just {uptime}.
BEFEHLE.ZAEHLEN_MUSTER:
It works best to keep counting and showing apart:
!death counts {deaths} up, moderators only, cooldown 0. Dying twice then counts twice.
!deaths counts nothing and just writes {deaths} into the reply. For everyone, with a few seconds of cooldown.
BEFEHLE.ABKUEHLUNG_TEXT: Without it, a single viewer can turn a command into a wall of text.
BEFEHLE.FERTIG_TEXT: Just switch them on. The text comes from the system.
BEFEHLE.FERTIG_ABKUEHLUNG: The cooldown of built-in commands is fixed. It depends not on taste but on what the command triggers ({{p}}clip about 60 seconds, because a real clip is created). For your own commands you set it yourself.
BEFEHLE.EIGENE_TEXT: A word, a reply, and who may use it.
BEFEHLE.LEER_TITEL: No command of your own yet
BEFEHLE.LEER_TEXT: Create one: you set the word, for example {{p}}rules, and the text the bot replies with.
BEFEHLE.ZAEHLER_TITEL: Which counter this command counts up
BEFEHLE.BAUSTEIN_FRAGE: Remove {{{name}}}? Texts that use it will show it literally afterwards.
BEFEHLE.BAUSTEINE_TEXT: Set once, use everywhere: in commands and announcements. If your invite changes, you change it in one place.
BEFEHLE.BAUSTEIN_LEER_TEXT: Create one, for example {discord} with your invite link. After that you can write it in any reply and any announcement.
BEFEHLE.NAME: Name
BEFEHLE.EINGEBAUT: Built-in names are taken: {spiel}, {rest} and the others above cannot be overwritten. A counter is counted up by a command; you choose which one on the command.

MITMACHEN.TITLE: Join in
MITMACHEN.SUBTITLE: What your viewers can trigger from chat.
MITMACHEN.CLIP_TEXT: !clip captures the last few seconds and posts the link in chat.
MITMACHEN.EINGERICHTET_NACH: . That page also shows who may use it.
MITMACHEN.CLIP_HINWEIS: Only while you are live: offline there is nothing to clip, and the bot says so in chat instead of asking Twitch. The finished clip takes a few seconds; the link goes out immediately and leads nowhere for a moment.
MITMACHEN.UMFRAGE_TEXT: Twitch's own polls: !umfrage says in chat how they stand.
MITMACHEN.AB_AFFILIATE: Polls require Affiliate status. Until then Twitch rejects creating them; that is their limit, not ours. Everything here stays in place and works the day you get the status, with nothing to set up again.
MITMACHEN.FREIGESCHALTET: Polls are enabled for your channel.
MITMACHEN.NICHT_NACHGESEHEN: We could not check with Twitch just now whether your channel may run polls. Twitch only allows them for Affiliates and Partners.
MITMACHEN.NEUE_UMFRAGE_TEXT: It appears in your stream immediately.
MITMACHEN.PUNKTE_NULL: 0 means no voting with channel points.
MITMACHEN.ZULETZT_TEXT: What Twitch still keeps. We add nothing to it.
MITMACHEN.VERLOSUNG_TEXT: !los enters a viewer in the running giveaway.
MITMACHEN.PLUGIN_NOETIG: This requires the Giveaways plugin to be active on this server.
MITMACHEN.MIT_BEDINGUNG: With a condition: anyone who does not meet it is told the reason in chat.
MITMACHEN.KEINE_VERLOSUNG: No giveaway is running that can be joined from the stream. That option is set when creating it.
MITMACHEN.LOS_HINWEIS: A viewer in chat needs no Discord account. Their entries are kept separately from the Discord participants, so they take up no slot the system was not made for. If they win, they are named in chat. !los replies in batches, not on every click: otherwise the bot would write fifty lines for fifty viewers.
MITMACHEN.MUSIK_1: !request, !song, !playlist, !vote, !skip, !prev: playback runs through a browser source in OBS, not through Discord.
MITMACHEN.MUSIK_2: Only your own uploaded library is played, and only files you have released for the stream.
MITMACHEN.GEHOERT_TITEL: None of this is ours. We only trigger it.
MITMACHEN.GEHOERT_1: A clip lives on Twitch's servers, a poll runs in Twitch's interface. We cut nothing ourselves and count no votes; we send the request and read the status. None of it is stored: once you close the page, nothing stays with us.
MITMACHEN.GEHOERT_2: That is also why there is no history of your polls here: what you see are the latest ones Twitch itself still keeps.
MITMACHEN.GEHOERT_3: The giveaway belongs to the giveaway plugin. It is created there, with prize, duration and conditions; this page only shows what currently reaches the chat. A second place to configure it would be a second truth, and the order of clicks would decide which one counts.

MUSIK.TITLE: Music requests
MUSIK.SUBTITLE: Whatever chat requests is played by a browser source in OBS.
MUSIK.KEINE_ABLAGE: No music library. The music plugin is not active in this guild, so there is nothing to play.
MUSIK.NICHT_FREI: No file released for the stream yet. Upload something under Music → Files and switch on "released for the stream". Until then !request finds nothing.
MUSIK.OBS_TEXT: In OBS: Add source → Browser, then paste this address. The sound comes from the browser source; Discord is not needed.
MUSIK.HAEKCHEN: Three checkboxes in the OBS dialog
MUSIK.HAKEN_1: "Control audio via OBS" → on. Otherwise the sound goes straight to the desktop device instead of getting its own channel in the audio mixer, with no fader and no mute.
MUSIK.HAKEN_2: "Shutdown source when not visible" → off. Otherwise the music stops at every scene change and the track starts over.
MUSIK.HAKEN_3: "Refresh browser when scene becomes active" → off. Same result by another route.
MUSIK.LAUTSTAERKE: You then set the volume in the audio mixer, where the source sits as its own channel next to microphone and game.
MUSIK.NUR_TON: Otherwise the source delivers sound only and stays invisible.
MUSIK.ADRESSE_GEHEIM: Anyone with this address can play your library. It is the browser source's only credential, so do not share it on stream or show it during setup.
MUSIK.ADRESSE_FRAGE: Create a new address? A browser source that is already running stops playing until you enter the new address in OBS.
MUSIK.BEENDEN_TEXT: Pauses and resets: the list then starts from the beginning. The queue stays.
MUSIK.ENDLOS_AN: When the queue is empty, a random released track plays on, never the same one twice in a row.
MUSIK.ENDLOS_AUS: Only what someone requests with !request plays. After that there is silence.
MUSIK.ENDE_AN: When the stream ends, this waits {{n}} minutes. If someone goes live again in that time, the music stays on; otherwise it stops and the queue stays. Every channel whose home guild is this guild counts. If no music is playing when the stream ends, nothing happens.
MUSIK.ENDE_AUS: The music keeps playing after the stream until someone pauses it.
MUSIK.EINREIHEN_TEXT: Appends all released tracks in random order.
MUSIK.BEFEHLE_TEXT: You set who may use them per command under My commands. The values here are the defaults.
MUSIK.T_REQUEST: Requests a track from the released library
MUSIK.T_STOP: Stops; the list then starts from the beginning
MUSIK.R_ADRESSE_NEU: New address created. Enter it in OBS.
MUSIK.R_ADRESSE_FEHLER: The address could not be renewed.
MUSIK.R_BEENDET: Stopped. The list starts from the beginning next time.
MUSIK.R_ENDLOS_AN: Endless on: it keeps playing, even without requests.
MUSIK.R_ENDLOS_AUS: Endless off: only requested tracks play now.
MUSIK.R_NACHLAUF: The delay must be between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes.
MUSIK.R_ENDE_AN: Saved. The music stops {{n}} minutes after the stream.
MUSIK.R_ENDE_AUS: Saved. The music keeps playing after the stream.
MUSIK.R_NICHTS_FREI: No file is released for the stream.
MUSIK.R_KEIN_PLUGIN: The music plugin is not active in this guild.
